Article Title: 'I apologise on his behalf': Tamil Nadu CM Vijay after minister's Karunanidhi reference
Article Text:
Vijay apologises on minister's behalf for his Karunanidhi reference

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tamil Nadu chief minister C Vijay Joseph apologised in the assembly on Monday after a minister referred to former CM and DMK patriarch late M Karunanidhi by name without using the customary respectful honorific.State forest minister R V Ranjith Kumar’s reference to the late DMK leader as “Karunanidhi”, without the traditional “Kalaignar” (scholar), triggered protests from opposition DMK members.Vijay intervened to defuse the tension, admitting that the reference was inappropriate and apologising on the minister’s behalf.“I apologise on his behalf,” Vijay said.The row erupted during a debate on demands for grants for the health and revenue departments. Ranjith Kumar was criticising alleged cash-for-votes practices and referred to the controversial “Thirumangalam formula”.He claimed that up to Rs 1,500 per vote had been distributed in his Kancheepuram constituency during previous elections. He contrasted this with the current government, saying it came to power without distributing money for votes.While referring to past election tactics, Ranjith Kumar mentioned Karunanidhi without the customary “Kalaignar” or “former chief minister” prefix. DMK members, led by former minister K K S S R Ramachandran, immediately protested, citing the assembly’s long-standing convention of using respectful titles for revered leaders.Vijay then halted the forest minister’s speech and intervened to prevent the protest from escalating, acknowledging that referring to the late leader without the customary honorific was inappropriate.
Article Summary: State forest minister R V Ranjith Kumar’s reference to the late DMK leader as “Karunanidhi’, without the traditional “Kalaignar’ (scholar) triggered protests from opposition DMK members. Chief minister C Vijay Joseph intervened to defuse the tension.

Article Title: 14 of 28 chief ministers face serious criminal cases, Supreme Court told
Article Text:
There are serious criminal cases against the chief ministers of 14 of the 28 states

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In the decade-old proceedings for expediting trials in criminal case against sitting/former MPs/MLAs, amicus curiae and senior advocate Vijay Hansaria has informed the Supreme Court that there are serious criminal cases against chief ministers of 14 of the 28 states, a list topped by Telangana's A Revanth Reddy who faces 89 cases.West Bengal's Suvendu Adhikari has 29 cases, Karnataka CM D Shivakumar 19, Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu 19, Kerala CM V D Satheesan 18 cases, Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren 5, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis 4, Himachal CM Sukhvinder Singh 4, TN CM C Joseph Vijay 2, Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary 2, and one each against other four - P S Tamang (Sikkim), Bhagwant Mann (Punjab), Mohan Charan Majhi (Odisha) and Bhajan Lal Sharma (Rajasthan).The maximum percentage of MLAs having serious criminal cases belong to Bengal - 170 out of 292 (58%). It is followed by Kerala 57%, Andhra Pradesh 56%, Telangana 49%, Jharkhand and Odisha 45% each, Bihar 42%. Maharashtra 40% and U%, the 96-page report filed by Hansaria revealed.In Lok Sabha, 170 MPs (31% of total strength of 543) have serious criminal cases pending against them. In Telangana 11 of the 17 MPs face serious criminal cases; in Kerala, 11 of its 21 MPS face serious criminal cases; in Bihar, 19 of the 40 MPs, in UP 34 of the 80 MPs.Maharashtra 17 of 48 MPs, Bengal 16 of the 42 MPs, and in Andhra Pradesh 9 of the 25 MPs face serious criminal cases.As of July 2026, as many as 4,192 criminal cases are pending trial against sitting/former MPs and MLAs, Hansaria said. Uttar Pradesh accounts for lion's share with 1,171 cases pending.In RS, 75 of 233 members (33%) have criminal cases against them, of which 40 (18%) cases are serious criminal cases (punishable with five years of imprisonment or more), the amicus report filed through advocate Sneha Kalita stated.The amicus requested the court to designate special courts to exclusively hold trial proceedings in cases against sitting and former legislators and direct the jurisdictional HCs to actively monitor progress in trials.
Article Summary: The maximum percentage of MLAs having serious criminal cases belong to Bengal - 170 out of 292 (58%). It is followed by Kerala 57%, Andhra Pradesh 56%, Telangana 49%, Jharkhand and Odisha 45% each, Bihar 42%. Maharashtra 40% and U%, the 96-page report filed by Vijay Hansaria revealed.

Article Title: 'Ready to show degree but ask pawpaw too': CJP chief Dipke amid row over Boston education
Article Text:
CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke offers to show his Boston University degree amid questions over his educational credentials.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) chief Abhijeet Dipke has offered to show his degree from Boston University amid questions over his educational background, while challenging Prime Minister Narendra Modi to do the same.Addressing the controversy in a social media post, Dipke said he was willing to provide documents to establish that he had attended the US university.“Hello everyone, I’ve been noticing for the last few days that people have been calling me a fraud and saying I never went to Boston University. I am ready to show my degree. But will your Pawpaw show his degree?” he said.“I am ready to show my degree but what about pawpaw? I am ready. I have all the documents,” he added.A community note attached to his post, however, said records relating to PM Modi's educational qualifications had already been made public.“Narendra Modi’s Bachelor’s and Master’s degree records have been publicly available for a considerable period of time,” the note said, while linking to a 2016 BJP post that showcased Modi's BA and MA degree records.In a separate post, Dipke drew a comparison between Boston University and Delhi University , asking why the latter had not highlighted PM Modi's association with the institution.“Boston University published an article about me for being their alumnus. Why doesn’t DU proudly celebrate Modi as their alumnus? He is, after all, the Prime Minister of India. Shouldn’t they be flexing about it instead of trying to hide his degree?” he said.This post also attracted a community note, which stated that Delhi University had published a list of Union cabinet ministers who were its alumni and that PM Modi was included in the list.Dipke has earlier said that he received a scholarship from Boston University and financed the remaining expenses through an education loan, which he is still repaying.The 30-year-old holds a Master of Science degree in Public Relations from Boston University. He returned to India in June and led the Cockroach Janta Party's agitation over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, with the protests eventually leading to the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke offers to show his Boston University degree amid questions over his educational credentials. He challenges Prime Minister Narendra Modi to do the same. A community note attached to his post, however, said records relating to PM Modi's educational qualifications had already been made public.

Article Text:
Former Union minister Smriti Irani has been appointed national general secretary, while former Rajasthan CM Vasundhara Raje Scindia, former Union minister D Purandeshwari and Uttar Pradesh MP Rekha Verma have been named national vice-presidents. (Photo: Agencies)

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday announced its new national team under party president Nitin Nabin , with 10 women and six leaders from minority communities finding a place among the national office-bearers.Former Union minister Smriti Irani has been appointed national general secretary, while former Rajasthan CM Vasundhara Raje Scindia, former Union minister D Purandeshwari, and Uttar Pradesh MP Rekha Verma have been named national vice-presidents.Kavita Patidar and Sangeeta Yadav will serve as national secretaries. Roop Kumari Choudhary has been appointed president of the BJP 's Mahila Morcha and Priti Gandhi has been made social media co-convenor.The new team also includes representatives from different minority communities. The BJP said it has accommodated one Sikh member, two Christian members and one member each from the Muslim, Jain and Parsi communities.Former Aligarh Muslim University vice-chancellor Prof Tariq Mansoor has been appointed national vice-president, while Kunwar Basit Ali will head the Minority Morcha as its president.Anil Antony, son of Congress veteran A K Antony, has been retained as a national secretary. Former Punjab finance minister Manpreet Singh Badal has been appointed national vice-president.According to the BJP, the new appointments provide representation to voices from 23 states and Union territories.The party described the team as a combination of administrative and organisational experience, youthfulness, geographical diversity and social inclusion."Such balanced appointments empower the incoming national president's executive team to operate with a profound awareness of the nation's vast geographical landscape and regional nuances," the BJP said in a statement.The party has also given special prominence to the North-East, appointing three regional leaders from Tripura, Assam and Nagaland while retaining the dedicated North-East Coordination Cell under Sambit Patra.The committee includes four tribal representatives from West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and the North-East, including two women. Three members from Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh represent the Scheduled Castes (SC).
Article Summary: Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday announced its new national team under party president Nitin Nabin. Former Union minister Smriti Irani has been appointed national general secretary. Former Rajasthan CM Vasundhara Raje Scindia, former Union minister D Purandeshwari and Uttar Pradesh MP Rekha Verma have been named national vice-presidents.

Article Title: Ram Mandir donation theft case: SC asks SIT to submit status report, take probe to logical end
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the special investigation team (SIT) to file a status report on the progress made in the Ram Temple donation theft probe and take the investigation to a logical conclusion.A bench CJI Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the SIT to take the probe to a logical conclusion and objectively consider any suggestions made by the litigants.The bench said after examining the report of the SIT, the court may issue certain directions for reforms in the management of donations made by the devotees visiting the Ram temple.While hearing petitions in the case, the apex court told the litigants that the SIT would consider only suggestions aimed at ensuring transparency and qualitative improvement in the probe.On July 27, the top court took note of the setting up of the four-member SIT headed by IGP Kiran S to probe the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple.The bench observed that “remedial actions will have to be taken” and said steps would be taken to “ensure transparency”.It also directed the SIT to submit a status report within two weeks.On July 20, the bench had asked the Uttar Pradesh government to apprise it about the possibility of setting up an SIT to probe the alleged embezzlement of donations.Earlier, on July 13, the bench had directed the Uttar Pradesh Police to submit a status report on the matter.The court had also issued notice to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on pleas seeking a fair and time-bound probe into the alleged donation theft.The pleas were filed after allegations of irregularities in the management of temple donations surfaced. Several petitioners, including RJD MP Sudhakar Singh, have sought a CBI probe and forensic audit of the temple trust’s finances. PTI
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the special investigation team (SIT) to file a status report on the progress made in the Ram Temple donation theft probe. A bench CJI Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the SIT to take the probe to a logical conclusion and objectively consider any suggestions made by the litigants.

Article Title: ‘Fake’ teacher appts: Probe schools run by netas & VVIPs too, says HC
Article Text:
The next hearing is on Sept 24

Mumbai:





Bombay HC has directed a special investigation team (SIT) formed by the state govt to probe alleged irregularities in appointments to educational institutions to turn the lens on all such institutes in every district of Maharashtra , including those run by a politician or a VVIP.Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad gave the direction on Aug 14 after they noticed that the SIT, which was earlier concentrating only on Nashik division, had started its investigations in various districts like Mumbai, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Amravati, Nagpur, Latur and Kolhapur.“We reiterate that the SIT shall investigate all educational institutions in every district of the state, irrespective of which management operates the said educational institutions or if any such institution is managed/conducted by any person, who is a people’s representative or is a VVIP,” the judges said.Several petitions were filed by assistant/deputy directors seeking framing of guidelines to protect employees/senior officers in the education department. HC in various orders had directed the state govt not to entertain complaints by strangers for against teachers and employees for cancelling their Shalarth ID or interfering with approvals granted years ago. Hence, the strangers started filing complaints against senior officers with police, who registered FIRs.Earlier this year, the state informed the court an SIT had been to investigate all appointments of teaching and non-teaching staff.Taking into account SIT’s interim report, the judges permitted it to “collate information, rather than believing rumours or baseless allegations”. Where persons unconnected with an institution have supplied material, the SIT shall ask them to file affidavits in support of their statements, they said. “The SIT would be at liberty to prosecute such a person for providing false information,” they added.The judges said the SIT could use information from a source to find out whether there are illegalities in recruitments and appointments and whether they “have caused loss to the state exchequer” as salary grants are paid from the “taxpayers’ pocket”. They posted the further hearing for Sept 24 to enable the state to indicate progress made by the SIT.
Article Summary: Bombay HC has directed a special investigation team (SIT) formed by the state govt to probe alleged irregularities in appointments to educational institutions. The SIT, which was earlier concentrating only on Nashik division, had started its investigations in various districts like Mumbai, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Amravati, Nagpur and Kolhapur.

Article Title: OBC activist booked by Jalna police over remarks on Maratha women, expresses regret later
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





OBC activist Navnath Waghmare was booked by the Jalna police on Monday for allegedly making objectionable remarks about women from the Maratha community during an interview aired on a YouTube channel.The case was registered at the Kadim Jalna police station following a complaint by Suvarna Wagh, a resident of Old Jalna. Members of the Maratha community also gathered outside the police station, raised slogans against Waghmare and demanded action.Deputy superintendent of police Anant Kulkarni said the FIR was registered under BNS sections 79, 196(1), 353(2) and 352 for allegedly insulting the modesty of women and promoting enmity between communities.According to the complaint, Waghmare made the comments while referring to BJP politician Chandrashekhar Bawankule’s remarks about his family. The complainant alleged that the remarks insulted Maratha women, hurt community sentiments and were intended to create tension between Marathas and OBCs.Following the backlash, Waghmare expressed regret over his comments. “I have never made such statements earlier.The remarks came while responding to criticism by Manoj Jarange against Chandrashekhar Bawankule. I appeal to women across the state to understand my position and forgive me,” he said.However, Waghmare also questioned when Jarange would apologise for his alleged remarks against NCP politician Chhagan Bhujbal, the Munde siblings, and the chief minister and deputy chief ministers.Jarange hit back, saying he never comments on women while speaking on community issues. “You have crossed all limits by speaking about Maratha women,” Jarange said, warning that those making such remarks would not be spared.Police said further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: Navnath Waghmare was booked by the Jalna police on Monday for allegedly making objectionable remarks about women from the Maratha community. The case was registered following a complaint by Suvarna Wagh, a resident of Old Jalna. The complainant alleged that the remarks insulted Maratha women, hurt community sentiments and were intended to create tension.

Article Title: Samant, Lad providing financial support to Jarange: OBC activist Navnath Waghmare
Article Text:
Uday Samant

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





OBC activist Navnath Waghmare on Monday accused state industries minister and Shiv Sena leader Uday Samant, along with BJP MLC Prasad Lad, of providing financial support to Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange in order to sustain the quota agitation.Waghmare warned that Samant and Lad would be held accountable if the situation escalated into violence between the Maratha and OBC communities. Speaking to the reporters in Jalna, Waghmare further alleged that Samant was exploiting Jarange to politically target Shiv Sena leader Eknath Shinde , with ambitions of becoming deputy chief minister.He claimed that Samant is attempting to weaken Shinde’s political standing and is plotting to split a faction of Shiv Sena MLAs. “Samant is unstable in the Shinde faction and is dreaming of becoming the deputy CM. He is allegedly providing financial support to Jarange and asking him to target Shinde,” Waghmare said, adding that Samant had been in touch with the BJP and could soon join the party.Waghmare alleged that Samant was using his position as industries minister to provide crores of rupees to Jarange. "This was aimed at diminishing Shinde’s political influence before attempting to split a group of Shiv Sena legislators,” he said.Waghmare also targeted Lad, alleging that the latter aspired for a ministerial position and deliberately responded whenever Jarange criticised the CM to remain in the political spotlight. He alleged that Lad was also providing financial backing to Jarange.“Lad has accumulated enormous wealth through tenders given by state govt. The govt itself has nurtured this snake, which is now turning around to bite it,” Waghmare said.The OBC activist urged the state govt to keep a watch on Samant and Lad rather than focusing solely on Jarange. “If these two do not provide him financial support, Jarange cannot do anything,” he claimed.He added that Samant and Lad were being used to weaken OBC reservation and urged CM Devendra Fadnavis and both deputy chief ministers to remain cautious of their activities.Samant and Lad could not be reached for their comments on the allegations levelled against them.
Article Summary: OBC activist Navnath Waghmare accused state industries minister and Shiv Sena leader Uday Samant, along with BJP MLC Prasad Lad, of providing financial support to Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange. He warned that Samant and Lad would be held accountable if the situation escalated into violence between the Maratha and OBC communities.

Article Title: Prithviraj Chavan’s ‘Munde joining Congress’ claim refuted by Pankaja, Raut Weighs In
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A claim by former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan — that late BJP politician Gopinath Munde was planning to join Congress in 2011 — has triggered a political controversy, with BJP minister and Gopinath Munde's daughter Pankaja Munde dismissing the claim and Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut entering the debate.Speaking in Satara on Saturday, Chavan had said discussions to induct Munde into Congress had progressed significantly during his tenure as chief minister.“We had decided to bring her (Pankaja’s) father into Congress when I was chief minister and had obtained Sonia Gandhi 's approval too. Munde wanted a ministerial post as he would have had to resign and contest again, and feared BJP politicians from Nagpur would work against him,” Chavan said.Chavan claimed Munde, then a senior BJP functionary, was deeply unhappy within the saffron party and had held secret meetings with Congress office-bearers. “He came to meet me secretly in Delhi. Instead of staying at Maharashtra Sadan, I stayed in a private hotel. We held confidential meetings with Ahmed Patel. Munde was deeply unhappy at the time,” Chavan said.The former chief minister said the move ultimately did not materialise because the then prime minister, Dr Manmohan Singh , opposed the induction of a neta directly from the opposition.Chavan described assuring Munde of a ministerial position without first consulting Singh as the “biggest mistake” of his political career.Pankaja Munde, however, rejected claims that her father intended to leave BJP. “My father was born in a lotus, and rested in a lotus. Now that he is no longer alive, there is no point in engaging in such political discussions,” she told reporters in Beed on Saturday.Pankaja, however, said Chavan's remarks were not intended to disrespect her father and urged people not to misinterpret his statement.Meanwhile, Sanjay Raut said on Sunday that Munde might have avoided the circumstances he faced within BJP had he joined Congress. Raut also praised Singh for opposing such defections. “Manmohan Singh was against politicians switching parties in such a manner. Sharad Pawar too had offered a similar suggestion. Munde was being severely harassed by BJP. He was constantly subjected to mental trauma and insults,” Raut said.Gopinath Munde, a former deputy chief minister of Maharashtra and Union rural development minister, died in a road accident in New Delhi on June 3, 2014.
Article Summary: Former Maharashtra chief minister Prithviraj Chavan claims Gopinath Munde was planning to join Congress in 2011. Chavan said discussions to induct Munde into Congress had progressed significantly during his tenure as chief minister. Munde wanted a ministerial post as he would have had to resign and contest again, he said.

Article Title: Will request Sharad Pawar to enlighten Rahul Gandhi on benefits of ethanol policy to farmers: Mushrif
Article Text:
Hasan Mushrif

Kolhapur

:

Praises roads in Gujarat





NCP leader and state minister Hasan Mushrif on Monday said he would request NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar to help educate leader of opposition and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on the benefits of the ethanol blending policy for farmers.Mushrif was responding to questions about the Centre facing criticism from the opposition over ethanol blending in petrol. Recently, Gandhi released a video hinting that he would take up the ethanol issue.“Ethanol policy has benefited the sugar cane farmers. Mills are able to pay fair and remunerative prices (FRP) to farmers through revenue generated from ethanol sales. In Brazil, 100% blending is practiced. While there are complaints about mileage, these can be addressed,” Mushrif said.“Pawar had recently asked me to visit the farmers to see the technical experiments conducted to increase productivity. When I meet him, I will request him to enlighten Gandhi on how much the ethanol policy has benefited the farmers. I don’t understand what he hopes to achieve by causing losses to the farmers,” he added.The minister also said that Gandhi should stop calling PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah disrespectfully as both are much elder to him in age and the positions they hold.Talking about the road conditions in Nandurbar, district guardian minister Mushrif said, “I visit Nandurbar once or twice in a month. From Surat by road it takes three hours to reach Nandurbar. Of this two hour road is in Gujarat and the last one hour in Maharashtra. The roads in Gujarat are very good, but that one hour road in Nandurbar is in worst condition.”He added, “Therefore, I said I feel ashamed by the conditions of the roads in Nandurbar. Govts come and go, but everyone should think of using some sort of technology that stops roads from deteriorating during rainfall.”
Article Summary: Mushrif was responding to questions about the Centre facing criticism from the opposition over ethanol blending in petrol. Gandhi released a video hinting that he would take up the ethanol issue. Mushrif also said that Gandhi should stop calling PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah disrespectfully.

Article Title: Liquor worth Rs1.8 cr seized by Kolhapur police

Article Title: HC quashes FIR in leopard skin case, allows fresh proceedings
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





The Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court has quashed a 2022 FIR against two men allegedly found carrying leopard and other wildlife skins, ruling that the police head constable who lodged the complaint was not authorised to do so under section 55 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.Justice Abhay J Mantri, however, granted liberty to the competent authorities specified under section 55 to rectify the procedural defects and initiate fresh proceedings against the accused in accordance with the law.The FIR was registered against Bajirao Shripati Yadav and Bhramadev Shashikant Patil, both residents of Ajara tehsil, under sections 9, 39, 40, 43, 44 and 51 of the Act.The high court accepted the defence’s contention that section 55 bars courts from taking cognisance of offences under the Act unless a complaint is filed by an authorised official, such as the Director of Wildlife Preservation, the Chief Wildlife Warden or an officer specifically empowered for the purpose.The court relied on the Bombay high court’s ruling in Mannu Kaduba Gavane vs. State of Maharashtra (2016) and the Supreme Court’s decision in Elvish Yadav vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2026). It held that the special procedure prescribed under section 55 takes precedence over general criminal procedure and must be strictly followed.According to the case, Sambhaji Bhosale, head constable with Ispurli police station in Kolhapur’s Karvir tehsil, received information through an assistant police inspector that two men were allegedly planning to sell a leopard skin on Kolhapur-Gargoti Road near Dindnerli Phata.Bhosale led a police team that laid a trap and intercepted the suspects. A search allegedly led to the recovery of a leopard skin and the skins of other wild animals, following which the FIR was registered.“Nothing has been produced on record to indicate that Bhosale had authority to make a complaint as mandated in section 55 of the Act,” justice Mantri said in the order passed on Friday.The court observed that when a law prescribes a special procedural mechanism, it must be followed to the exclusion of general statutory provisions.
Article Summary: The Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court has quashed a 2022 FIR against two men allegedly found carrying leopard and other wildlife skins. The court ruled that the police head constable who lodged the complaint was not authorised to do so under section 55 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.

Article Title: Ambernath BJP-MNS clash: Case registered against 2 BJP corporators, five others
Article Text:
A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash.





AMBERNATH: The political clash between BJP and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers in Ambernath has taken a fresh turn, with Shivaji Nagar police registering a fresh case against seven people, including two BJP corporators, on the complaint of an MNS worker who was injured in the incident.The latest case was registered on Sunday on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash. Police have booked BJP corporators Abhijit Karanjule and Pawan Walekar along with five others under sections 118(1), 115(2), 189(2), 190, 191(2) and 324(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The development comes days after police arrested Shirke and some of his associates for allegedly assaulting BJP office-bearer Laxmi Narayan Chauhan at his office in Vadavali.A subsequent clash between BJP and MNS workers at Shivaji Nagar police station further escalated tensions.MNS leaders had alleged that police took one-sided action by arresting their office-bearers while failing to act against BJP workers allegedly involved in the assault on Shirke. MNS leader Avinash Jadhav had demanded action against those responsible.Following the demand, MNS district president Bandu Deshmukh had announced a protest on Sunday against what the party termed one-sided police action. However, after police registered an FIR against BJP workers, MNS withdrew its protest.
Article Summary: A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash. The latest case was registered on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash.

Article Title: Don’t destroy Pune’s hills for road projects, says Supriya
Article Text:
NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule

​Pune:





Baramati MP and working president of NCP (SP) Supriya Sule on Monday said that her party will oppose hill cutting and for road projects in Pune, including the Patal Lok project.​“We are not against development, but it should not come at the cost of environment,” she said, adding that they have also opposed the Balbharati to Paud Phata road. She was speaking to reporters after a visit to Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC).​Supriya said that hill cutting should stop immediately and warned that her party’s members, both political workers and residents, will take to the streets against such destruction.She said the appointment of BJP functionary Girish Mahajan as Nashik’s guardian minister was wrong, given the allegations of corruption and fake tenders surrounding the Kumbh event. “PM Narendra Modi promised us ‘Na Khaunga, Na Khane Dunga’. He should look into Maharashtra and the corruption here,” she said.​The MP called for a review of tribal schools and urged MPs and MLAs to inspect ashramshalas in their jurisdictions, suggesting the use of CSR funds where needed.Supriya said the state govt has failed in urbanisation and in addressing civic issues despite being in power for seven years. During her meeting with PMC officials, she brought up potholes, garbage, property tax in merged areas, pollution in Undri, construction on a nullah in Bavdhan, and power disruptions in Dhayari.​Sule also said govt has failed to tackle paper leaks and that NEP has not delivered, adding that special efforts must be made to help Marathi schools survive. She also questioned why the industry department was not rolling out the red carpet for industries.On allegations that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi opposed ‘Vande Mataram’, Sule said that she could not confirm the authenticity of the video. She said govt should clarify its stand on Ayodhya Ram Temple issues and reveal who ordered the firing on agitators at Jantar Mantar during the recent CJP protests.​On autorickshaw drivers learning Marathi, Sule said it will help customer-friendly service.Her party workers protested over poor roads, hyacinth-clearance tenders, and recurring flood risks along Sinhagad Road and the proposal to rename the mayor’s residence on Ghole Road.Shrikant Patil, city unit chief of NCP (SP), said, “Massive potholes are endangering lives. The ruling party recently approved a tender to clear hyacinth from Mula-Mutha river that heavy rainfall and water discharge had already washed away, making the fresh expenditure wasteful. A thorough inquiry is a must.”
Article Summary: Baramati MP and working president of NCP (SP) Supriya Sule on Monday said that her party will oppose hill cutting and for road projects in Pune. She was speaking to reporters after a visit to Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC)

Article Title: Pune court grants anticipatory bail to advocate for objectionable social media post on PM Modi
Article Text:
The complainant alleged that the social media post on PM Modi had the potential to disturb public peace

Pune:





A court has granted anticipatory bail to advocate Amol Ankush Gavhane in a case registered over a social media post that allegedly featured a photograph of Prime Minister Narendra Modi with an objectionable caption.The case stems from a complaint filed by advocate Basvaraj Mallikarjun Yatwad, who alleged that he came across a social media on July 21 on an account purportedly belonging to Gavhane. Yatwad alleged that the post had the potential to disturb public peace.Additional sessions judge AV Chaudhari-Inamdar passed the order on Aug 14 in a case registered at Pune’s Cyber police station under sections 336(2), 353(1)(B) and 356(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Appearing for Gavhane, advocate Milind Pawar submitted that his client had cooperated fully with the investigation and that custodial interrogation was unnecessary. The court noted that Gavhane had complied with a notice issued under Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), appeared before the investigating officer and that his cellphone had already been seized while his statement had been recorded.Opposing the plea, the prosecution informed the court that details from the parent company regarding the social media account were still awaited and that efforts were under way to trace the person who had allegedly sent the disputed photograph to Gavhane.The court observed that the investigation officer had not asserted the need for Gavhane’s custodial interrogation. It also took note of the fact that he had no criminal antecedents and held that the remaining aspects of the investigation could be addressed through appropriate bail conditions.Accordingly, the court directed that Gavhane be released on anticipatory bail upon furnishing a personal recognisance bond of Rs 25,000 along with one or two sureties of the like amount.
Article Summary: The case stems from a complaint filed by advocate Basvaraj Mallikarjun Yatwad, who alleged that he came across a social media on July 21 on an account purportedly belonging to Amol Ankush Gavhane. The complainant alleged that the post had the potential to disturb public peace.

Article Title: 21 stray dogs, 2 cats allegedly poisoned in Nashik village, 2 booked
Article Text:
Police booked two Lohoner village residents for allegedly poisoning stray animals (File Photo)





NASHIK: In a case of animal cruelty, the Deola police have booked two residents of Lohoner village in Nashik district for allegedly poisoning 21 stray dogs and two cats earlier this week.The accused have been identified as Ramesh Ahire and Mukesh, alias Papa Pardeshi. An FIR was registered on Aug 14 under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, and the Maharashtra Police Act.According to the police, information was received on the morning of Aug 13 about the deaths of several stray animals near the Balaji temple and the Maharashtra Bank areas of Lohoner village. Inspector Sarthak Nehete, assistant Inspector Vinay Devre and constable Suresh Ramesh Korade visited the spot.During the investigation, the police found that the accused had allegedly purchased raw chicken from a local butcher around 7.30pm on Aug 12 and later bought toxic pesticides from a nearby shop. The pesticide was allegedly mixed with the chicken and fed to stray dogs and cats at different locations in the village.On the morning of Aug 13, sanitation worker Kantilal Salunkhe found 20 dogs and two cats dead. Unaware of police procedures, he collected the carcasses and buried them in a pit behind the village Amrutdham ground using a JCB machine.While inspecting the area, the police reportedly saw another dog foaming at the mouth and writhing in pain before collapsing. The animal was immediately taken to the Deola veterinary hospital for postmortem and sample collection.Following the postmortem findings and verification of the burial site, constable Korade lodged the complaint against the two accused. The police said the accused deliberately laced chicken pieces with poison and fed them to the animals. Inspector Sarthak Nehete is conducting further investigation.
Article Summary: Deola police have booked two residents of Lohoner village for allegedly poisoning 21 stray dogs and two cats. The accused have been identified as Ramesh Ahire and Mukesh, alias Papa Pardeshi. The police said the accused deliberately laced chicken pieces with poison and fed them to the animals.

Article Title: AIADMK MLAs’ resignation accepted only after inquiry, speaker tells HC
Article Text:
TN assembly

Chennai:





The resignation letters of six AIADMK MLAs were accepted only after conducting an inquiry to ascertain whether they had resigned voluntarily, Tamil Nadu Assembly speaker J C D Prabhakar has informed Madras high court “The MLAs submitted resignation letters written in their own handwriting. I conducted inquiries with each of them. I accepted the letters only after satisfying myself that the resignations were made of their own free will, the speaker said through his counter affidavit filed in response to a plea moved by AIADMK whip Afri S S Krishnakurthy challenging the speaker’s decision.He contended that the acceptance of the resignations was legally valid. He sought appropriate orders to dismiss the petitions challenging his decision.Recording the submissions, the first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan, adjourned the hearing to Sept 1.According to the petitioner, the speaker has chosen not to appear before the court even after he was issued a notice. Instead, the Assembly secretary filed a counter-affidavit stating that she was authorized to do so on behalf of the speaker.Claiming that the resignations were accepted at ‘lightning speed’, the petitioner said the speaker had completely ignored his constitutional duty of holding an inquiry before accepting the resignations, as he was in possession of information that the MLAs had violated the party whip.
Article Summary: The resignation letters of six AIADMK MLAs were accepted only after conducting an inquiry to ascertain whether they had resigned voluntarily. Tamil Nadu Assembly speaker J C D Prabhakar has informed Madras high court “The MLAs submitted resignation letters written in their own handwriting. I conducted inquiries with each of them,” he said.

Article Title: Four vehicles involved in illegal sand mining seized in Krishnagiri, probe on
Article Text:
Those engaged in the illegal activity, abandoned the vehicles and fled on seeing the police approaching

Krishnagiri:





An earthmover and three tractors which were involved in illegal sand mining near Nagarasampatty in Krishnagiri district, were seized during the early hours of Monday.According to an officer, sand was being illegally excavated from the Nagaleri Lake under Avathuvadi panchayat around 2am on Monday. Acting on a tip-off, the village administrative officer S Dinesh inspected the site and confirmed that sand was being loaded into three tractors with the help of an earthmover.“Nagarasampatty police reached the spot based on his information. However, those engaged in the illegal activity, abandoned the vehicles and fled on seeing the police approaching,” the officer said.A case has been registered, and police are investigating further to trace and arrest the absconding culprits.(Photos: S Parthiban)
Article Summary: An earthmover and three tractors which were involved in illegal sand mining near Nagarasampatty in Krishnagiri district, were seized during the early hours of Monday. According to an officer, sand was being illegally excavated from the Nagaleri Lake under Avathuvadi panchayat.

Article Title: Coimbatore district police arrest man for derogatory posts about Lord Murugan
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Periyanaickenpalayam police in Coimbatore district arrested a man on charges of posting derogatory comments about Hindu deity Lord Murugan on social media.Police arrested Michael of Rakkipalayam based on a complaint filed by M Shankar, who is the Narasimhanaickenpalayam union general secretary of Hindu Munnani. He alleged that Michael, through posts on Instagram and Facebook, used offensive words and made disparaging remarks targeting Lord Murugan that could disturb public peace and incite religious tension.Based on the complaint, police registered a case and arrested Michael, who is a TVK supporter.Cases were registered against Michael in several districts on the same issue, police sources said. Officials from the respective district police units have contacted the Coimbatore district police to coordinate efforts to arrest him.
Article Summary: Police arrested Michael of Rakkipalayam based on a complaint filed by M Shankar, who is the Narasimhanaickenpalayam union general secretary of Hindu Munnani. He alleged that Michael used offensive words and made disparaging remarks targeting Lord Murugan.

Article Title: Former TVK candidate Arun Kumar joins AIADMK
Article Text:
Salem





: Former TVK candidate M Arun Kumar on Saturday joined AIADMK after meeting party general secretary and former chief minister Edappadi K Palaniswami at the latter’s residence here.Arun Kumar, who had earlier served as the AIADMK union councillor in Ayothiapattinam, later joined TVK. He was initially announced as the TVK candidate in the Edappadi assembly constituency. His nomination was rejected after election officials found that the proposers listed in his papers could not be verified. The substitute candidate’s papers were also rejected on similar grounds, leaving TVK without a contender against Palaniswami in the constituency.By joining the AIADMK, Arun Kumar shifted political loyalties, strengthening the party’s grassroots presence in Salem district.(Photos: TOI)
Article Summary: Arun Kumar had earlier served as the AIADMK union councillor in Ayothiapattinam. He was initially announced as the TVK candidate in the Edappadi assembly constituency. His nomination was rejected after election officials found that the proposers listed in his papers could not be verified.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: MDMA, synthetic drugs worth Rs 1 cr seized; 3 held
Article Text:
AI-image

Palakkad

:





Police seized around one kilogram of MDMA and other synthetic drugs worth an estimated Rs 1 crore and arrested three people, including a couple, at Olavakkode on Monday.The arrested have been identified as Muhammad Nishi, 26, a native of Kanjirappally in Kottayam; Muhammad Asurudeen , 30, a native of Vengara in Malappuram; and his wife, Bee Fathima, 27, a native of Dakshina Kannada in Karnataka. The couple and their friend were allegedly transporting the drugs in an Innova car when they were intercepted by the Palakkad North police at Olavakkode.Besides MDMA, police also seized cocaine, hybrid ganja and LSD stamps from the accused. Police said the drugs were brought to Kerala from Bengaluru for special sales during the Onam season. The accused allegedly used an Innova rented from Tamil Nadu to transport the contraband.Police said the three were habitual drug traffickers and suspect the involvement of a larger drug trafficking network. Investigators are probing the source of the drugs, their intended distribution network and the possible involvement of other members of the alleged racket.
Article Summary: Police seized around one kilogram of MDMA and other synthetic drugs worth an estimated Rs 1 crore. The arrested have been identified as Muhammad Nishi, 26, a native of Kanjirappally in Kottayam; Muhammad Asurudeen, 30, and his wife, Bee Fathima, 27. The couple and their friend were allegedly transporting the drugs in an Innova car.

Article Title: Muthanga stir: Kerala HC reserves order in Geethanandan’s plea for suspension of jail term and bail
Article Text:
HC

Kochi

:





The high court on Monday reserved its order on a petition filed by Adivasi Gothra Maha Sabha (AGMS) co-founder M Geethanandan and three other convicts in the case arising from the 2003 Muthanga agitation, seeking suspension of their sentences and grant of bail.The bench of Justice A Badharudeen also admitted their appeal and adjourned it for further hearing. During Monday’s hearing, senior counsel for the CBI submitted that the agency would also appeal against certain adverse remarks made against its investigating team in the trial court judgment.The case stems from the 2003 Muthanga agitation, in which the appellants, along with other AGMS members, allegedly trespassed into the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary. During the subsequent eviction drive, they allegedly attacked police and forest officials and took two police personnel and a forest official hostage. Police constable Vinod and an activist, Yogi, were killed in the incident. The Kalpetta sessions court, while acquitting 53 accused, had convicted Geethanandan, Binu, Ramesan and Anil Kumar and sentenced them to five years’ imprisonment for various offences, including unlawful assembly, rioting while armed with deadly weapons, kidnapping and attempt to murder.The appellants moved HC contending that the trial court had convicted and sentenced them based only on its observation that the offence of criminal conspiracy under Section 120B of the IPC was prima facie attracted against them, without recording a conclusive finding that the offence had been proved. They also submitted that the trial court had erred in convicting them without invoking Section 149 of the IPC, which fixes criminal liability on every member of an unlawful assembly for offences committed in prosecution of its common object.
Article Summary: The high court reserved its order on a petition filed by Adivasi Gothra Maha Sabha (AGMS) co-founder M Geethanandan. The case stems from the 2003 Muthanga agitation, in which the appellants, along with other AGMS members, allegedly trespassed into the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary.
